title: ProjectE DRC/ERC comparability verdict
description: Output of `drc_gate.py --compare LEFT RIGHT`. Two DRC counts are only a measurement together when the engine version and the invocation flags behind them are both KNOWN and EQUAL. The case that produced this schema: a committed drc.json recorded 191 violations / 21 unconnected under kicad-cli 10.0.5; the same unchanged board under 10.0.4 returned a different number, the board digest was identical, and nothing refused to subtract the two. A difference that cannot be attributed to the design or to the tool is not a measurement.

blockers.description: Empty exactly when verdict is COMPARED. Every entry is a reason these two numbers may not be subtracted.

design_changed.description: null when either side carries no design digest (a raw kicad-cli report never does), so the delta cannot be pinned on anything.

attribution.description: What the delta is attributable to. 'design' = the digests differ, which is the legitimate reason to compare. 'none_expected' = the SAME board digest, so any non-zero delta is the run-to-run nondeterminism drc_gate.py::build_argv documents, not progress. 'unknown' = no digest to compare.

delta.description: right minus left, per metric. MUST be null when verdict is REFUSED: publishing '191 vs 222 = 31' is exactly the unattributable number this tool exists to withhold.

agreement.description: Only meaningful when attribution is 'none_expected': true when an unchanged design produced identical counts, false when it did not. null otherwise - a design that legitimately changed is neither in nor out of agreement.

inputs.description: Present when the two reports were read from disk: path plus digest of each, so the verdict is bound to the bytes it was computed from.

engine_version.description: null when the artefact carries no usable version. Two nulls are two unanswered questions, never one matching answer, so they are refused rather than treated as equal.

argv_signature.description: null for a raw kicad-cli report: it records the KiCad version but never the command line, so whether it was produced with --all-track-errors (worth ~100 violations on this repo's board) is unknowable from the file.

$comment: Exit codes: 0 comparable and in agreement, 1 comparable and an unchanged design produced two different answers, 2 REFUSED. 2 rather than 1 for a refusal is deliberate and follows common/report_io: 1 means the tool ran and the answer is no, 2 means the tool could not produce an answer. A gate that maps a refusal onto 1 cannot tell a regression from an unanswerable question.
